newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries carry over easier tone in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries carry over easier tone in Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries carried over the easier tone from overnight by Tokyo midday on Tuesday due to light follow-through profit-taking, traders said.
"Treasuries drifted down slightly as there are profit-taking needs, but sharp falls are unlikely from the current levels," a senior U.S. brokerage trader said.
Attention in the market was shifting to quarterly refunding, which the Treasury will kick off with the sale of $16 billion in three-year notes later in the day, traders said.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 101-27/32, yielding 6.48 percent, compared with 101-29/32 in New York on Monday.
"I expect there to be strong demand from investors (in the three-year note auction) if the yield stays above 6.0 percent," the trader said.
The three-year note was at around 6.01 percent in when-issued trading in the morning.
The Treasury will offer $12 billion in 10-year notes on Wednesday followed by the auction of $10 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
Traders said the demand was expected to be strong should the yield of the 10-year note be around 6.25 percent, and around 6.5 percent for the 30-year bond.

Operators have turned cautious about the trend of the market since Friday's plunge in reaction to stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs data and the National Association of Purchasing Management report that suggested the U.S. manufacturing sector was strong.
But many operators were still eager to buy on dips.
"Prices collapsed last Friday, but many participants saw the falls as a part of correction as recent rises had been extremely rapid," a Japanese brokerage trader said.
"We have to watch the results of the auction, but I expect bargain-hunters may emerge very soon," the trader said.
Many Japanese institutional investors continued to take a wait-and-see attitude on a belief that the dollar was unlikely to climb sharply on concerns over possible verbal intervention.

"(Japanese) fund managers are expected to be keen about buying Treasuries should the yield (of the 30-year bond) climb back above 6.5 percent," the Japanese brokerage trader said. "They may actually start purchasing after confirming the trend of the market following the auction," he said.
The September T-bond futures contract rose 2/32 to 114-22/32. The contract was moving in a range of 114-19/32 to 114-24/32. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
